results.title: Spatial and temporal context: Significance and symbolism
results.content: # Significance of Spatial and temporal context. Spatial and temporal context, as defined in Environmental Sciences, involves the location and timeframe where events take place. This context significantly shapes vegetation change patterns. Recurrent models integrate these contexts to predict future locations, improving forecast accuracy. These models consider both geographical proximity and time-dependent movement patterns. Understanding spatial and temporal context is crucial for analyzing environmental processes and predicting future changes. Synonyms: Context, Setting, Background, Environment, Situation, Frame of reference, Geographic context, Historical context, Situational context. The below excerpts are indicatory and do represent direct quotations or translations. It is your responsibility to fact check each reference. ## The concept of Spatial and temporal context in scientific sources. Spatial and temporal context involves location and time frame, influencing vegetation change patterns. Integrated into models, it enhances forecasting accuracy by considering geographical proximity and time-dependent movement patterns. (1) Spatial and temporal contexts are integrated into recurrent models to predict the next location, enhancing the accuracy of forecasting by considering both the geographical proximity and the time-dependent patterns of movement. (2) It refers to the location and time frame in which events occur, influencing patterns of vegetation change.

results.content: # Comparing sampling patterns for kriging the spatial mean temporal trend. In this article, the best linear unbiased predictor of the spatial mean temporal trend and its variance are derived under a universal kriging model. For small spatial ranges, the time-separation pattern is optimal, regardless of the temporal range. 1/4 of the spatial range) the serially alternating pattern is best, whereas the time-separation pattern is best for larger temporal ranges. Unless one has good knowledge of the spatial and temporal range, the serially alternating pattern is thus a good choice. ## Access this article. results.title: Microsoft Teams gets support for Spatial Audio - Windows 10 Forums
results.content: # Microsoft Teams gets support for Spatial Audio # Microsoft Teams gets support for Spatial Audio >  Teams Spatial Audio aligns the perceived audio location of each participant with their video representation to make it easier for users to track who is speaking, to understand better when multiple speakers are speaking at the same time, and to lower meeting fatigue and cognitive load. > * Currently we support wired headsets for spatial audio. > * Native Bluetooth devices do not support stereo during a call, therefore spatial audio is available. For these devices, spatial audio will be supported. Currently, spatial audio is not supported for users on satellite server. In future releases, all users will be supported for spatial audio. > * Users can turn on music mode while receiving spatial audio. Future releases will support receiving music mode in spatial audio.

results.title: Spatial and temporal filtering methods | Brain-Computer Interfaces Class Notes
results.content: ## 🧠Brain-Computer Interfaces Unit 6 Review. ## 6.2 Spatial and temporal filtering methods. ## 🧠Brain-Computer Interfaces Unit 6 Review. # 6.2 Spatial and temporal filtering methods. Written by the Fiveable Content Team • Last updated September 2025. Written by the Fiveable Content Team • Last updated September 2025. ###### Unit & Topic Study Guides. 6.1 Signal preprocessing techniques. 6.2 Spatial and temporal filtering methods. Spatial filtering enhances EEG data by improving signal-to-noise ratio and separating brain activity from artifacts. Common Spatial Patterns (CSP) technique maximizes variance between classes, optimizing signal separation for tasks like motor imagery in BCIs. Temporal filtering modifies frequency content, removing unwanted components and isolating relevant brain rhythms. Methods include moving average, exponential smoothing, bandpass, and notch filtering. ## Spatial Filtering Techniques. ### Spatial and temporal filtering concepts. * Spatial filtering enhances specific spatial patterns in multichannel EEG data improving signal-to-noise ratio and separating brain activity from artifacts based on volume conduction principle in the brain. * Temporal filtering modifies frequency content of time-domain signals removing unwanted components and isolating relevant brain rhythms (alpha, beta, gamma) utilizing frequency-domain transformations (Fourier, wavelet). ### Common Spatial Patterns technique. * CSP maximizes variance of one class while minimizing another optimizing signal separation for classification tasks. 2. Perform generalized eigenvalue decomposition. 3. Select spatial filters based on eigenvalues. * Widely applied in motor imagery-based BCIs enhancing discrimination between left and right hand movements. ### Temporal filtering methods. * Moving average filter calculates average of fixed-size window smoothing data and reducing noise (rectangular, Hamming windows). * Exponential smoothing assigns decreasing weights to older observations $S\_t = α \* Y\_t + (1 - α) \* S\_{t-1}$ where $α$ is smoothing factor. * Bandpass filtering isolates specific frequency bands relevant to BCI paradigms (alpha: 8-13 Hz, beta: 13-30 Hz). * Notch filtering removes power line interference preserving signal integrity (50 Hz in Europe, 60 Hz in USA). ### Effects of filters on performance. * Performance metrics evaluate filter effectiveness (classification accuracy, information transfer rate, SNR). * Feature selection methods optimize filter output (correlation-based, recursive feature elimination). * Filter parameter optimization improves performance (grid search, genetic algorithms). * Filter design involves trade-offs between spatial/temporal resolution and computational complexity.
